title: Bandwidth-tiered fidelity: SDK shims for offload-first streaming (PRD draft)
content:
Executive summary:
This draft proposes a pragmatic SDK-level pattern and small hosted-API surface changes to support bandwidth-tiered progressive fidelity for streaming responses and tool calling. The goal is to let clients explicitly (and cheaply) trade fidelity for bandwidth and latency while maintaining strong semantics for tool calls and structured output.

Why this matters (problem statement):
- Mobile and constrained-edge clients (phone, intermittent networks, embedded webviews) struggle with large streamed payloads from hosted LLM responses, especially when tool calls produce bulky attachments (tables, images, JSON payloads).
- Current approach (always-stream full fidelity) forces either heavy client-side logic or server-side one-size-fits-all throttling, which causes wasted tokens or poor UX.
- Developers end up putting brittle heuristics into their apps. We should expose intentional, observable knobs so teams can design for graceful fidelity degradation.

Principles / success criteria:
- Explicit: SDK/HTTP surface must make fidelity tiers and their fallbacks explicit, not implicit magic.
- Incremental: Backwards compatible for existing clients; default behavior identical to today if not opted-in.
- Composable with tool-calls: Tool invocations (and attachments) must flow through tier decisions without breaking idempotency or observability.
- Observable & billable: Telemetry must tie tier selection to token counts and latency for cost attribution and debugging.

Goals (MVP):
1) Define 3 fidelity tiers: compact, normal, verbose.
   - compact: minimal text output, structured summaries only, no heavy attachments (attachments suppressed or replaced by artifact references).
   - normal: current default behavior (unchanged streaming semantics).
   - verbose: include optional attachments, extended explanations, developer notes.
2) Introduce an SDK shim that negotiates fidelity on stream handshake and provides local hooks to progressively materialize higher-fidelity content as network permits.
3) Ensure tool calls and structured JSON outputs are preserved in compact tier via compressed or truncated representations + schema-delta references.
4) Add telemetry events: fidelity-requested, fidelity-negotiated, fidelity-upgrade-attempt, tool-attachment-evicted.

Non-goals (for MVP):
- Automatic semantic compression of user prompts/responses via ML summarization (future).
- Full new billing model (we will surface usage but keep billing as existing token counts for now).

User stories:
- Mobile product manager: "I want the chat to appear instantly on flaky cellular networks with a compact summary, but be able to fetch the full result if the user taps 'expand'."
- Marketplace integration: "We need deterministic tool-call outputs even when attachments are trimmed, so we can reconcile results later."
- Platform engineer: "I want to trace which fidelity tier caused an error and what tokens were billed."

Design overview:
1) Client -> Server handshake extension (streaming socket or HTTP upgrade):
   - New optional headers / handshake JSON: fidelity_preference [compact|normal|verbose], prefetch_budget_ms (client-suggested local prefetch time budget), allow_attachment_eviction [true|false].
   - Server responds with fidelity_granted and list of accepted constraints and rationale (server_tier, fallback_reasons).
   - If server grants compact but determines a tool-call will emit an attachment, server returns a tool-attachment-policy for that request (embed|link|evict).

2) Streaming wire format (small additive changes):
   - Add frame type: fidelity_hint (sparse), fidelity_commit, attachment_manifest.
   - Attachment_manifest contains an artifact id, size_hint, mime, and compressed_summary (compact tier must get compressed_summary).
   - Clients can request on-demand attachment_fetch by artifact id (separate authenticated fetch endpoint; optional pricing note).

3) SDK shim behaviors (recommended reference SDK change):
   - On handshake, SDK exposes an API surface: setFidelityPreference(), onFidelityNegotiated(callback), onAttachmentManifest(callback).
   - Provide built-in offline-first cache: when compact content received, SDK queues background fetches for artifacts when connected to WiFi or above threshold bandwidth.
   - Provide graceful UI helpers: getExpandableSummary(), isAttachmentAvailable(artifactId), fetchAttachment(artifactId, priority).

4) Tool call semantics and structured output preservation:
   - All tool-call results must include a tooling_trace header (trace id + minimal metadata) embedded even in compact tier. This guarantees reconciliation.
   - For structured JSON outputs, server will always stream a compact schema-delta summary when in compact tier; the full JSON may be swapped for an artifact reference.
   - Tool calls that mutate external state (webhooks, DB writes) are unaffected by fidelity tier; we must ensure idempotency and confirm commits in the stream (commit frames).

API sketches (HTTP & streaming examples):
- Client request header snippet: "X-RW-Fidelity: compact;prefetch_ms=150;attachment_eviction=true"
- Server handshake response: {
  "fidelity_granted": "compact",
  "attachment_policy": "link-if-large"
}
- Stream frame examples (pseudo):
  - "fidelity_hint: compact-summary"
  - "attachment_manifest: {id: art_123, size: 1.2MB, mime: \"application/json\", summary: \"table 5 rows, key metrics\"}"

Billing and telemetry notes:
- For MVP, billing unchanged. We will annotate billing reports with fidelity tier to enable later pricing experiments.
- Telemetry: sample fidelity adoption rate, time-to-first-byte for compact vs normal, attachment-evictions-per-1000-requests, per-request token counts, latencies.
- Tracing: ensure tooling_trace id links to SLO traces and can be searched in the Console.

SDK ergonomics & migration plan (developer-facing):
- Backwards compatible defaults: if SDK does not opt into handshake headers, server behaves as today.
- Migration guide: short code examples in JS/Go/Python to opt-in and wire up expand-on-demand UI.
- Developer checklist: ensure UI affordances for 'more' button, handle partial structured JSON gracefully, test idempotent tool-call replay.

Operational and edge cases:
- Mid-stream upgrade attempt: client attempts to upgrade fidelity (client has more bandwidth) -> server will accept if resources permit and stream fidelity_commit frames with delta. Otherwise server sends fidelity_deny with reason code. SDK exposes onFidelityChange(reason).
- Attachment eviction race: if a client requests an evicted artifact concurrently with server GC, server returns 404 + eviction_reason; SDK should attempt background reconciliation via artifact index (retry policy).
- Tool-call side effects: ensure commit frames are delivered even when streaming in compact mode; if commit frame fails to reach client (network cut), server retains commit status in trace and exposes fetch_commit_status endpoint.

Observability & test plan:
- Add unit and integration tests for handshake permutations (compact->normal->verbose upgrades and downgrades).
- Simulated flaky network harness (existing hosted-api integration lab) to measure time-to-first-summary and expansion click latency.
- Console: per-route fidelity heatmap and artifact-eviction counts, plus quick links from traces to artifact manifests.

Rollout plan:
- Canary 1 (internal apps): enable fidelity handshake for internal Redwood Console clients only, no billing change, add telemetry. (~2 weeks)
- Canary 2 (beta SDK opt-in customers): release SDK shim as alpha, allow customers to opt into compact/normal. Monitor error rates and tool-call reconciliation. (~4 weeks)
- Gradual opt-in: default remains unchanged. After 8–12 weeks evaluate telemetry and consider offering Fideltiy as stable feature or new billing tier.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should artifact fetches be charged differently or have rate limits? (billing team)
- How do we guarantee schema-delta patching across model versions? (research/ML + infra)
- Best-effort vs strict attachment guarantees for regulated workflows (private deployments may require always-include attachments).
- UX: do we provide server-side heuristics to auto-select fidelity based on observed RTT/bandwidth? (ops/ML experiment)

Appendix: quick example flow (mobile):
1) Mobile app calls createChat() with X-RW-Fidelity: compact;prefetch_ms=200
2) Server streams compact summary frame within 120ms. UI shows instant summary.
3) Server sends attachment_manifest for a large table as artifact art_123 with compressed_summary. UI shows "download details" CTA.
4) User taps expand -> SDK fetchAttachment(art_123) which hits artifact endpoint (GET /v1/artifacts/art_123). If on WiFi, SDK fetches eagerly; otherwise queues.

Notes to reviewers:
- Focus feedback on wire frame primitives and whether the compact tier semantics are sufficient to preserve tool-call determinism.
- Flag any security concerns around artifact references (link-only mode) — we probably need short-lived signed URLs for explicit fetch.
- Mark any Console UX needs (heatmaps, artifact browser) so we can scope Console tickets.

Author notes / rough TODOs in doc body:
- [ ] Add proto/avro example of attachment_manifest schema.
- [ ] Draft SDK JS reference implementation sketch.
- [ ] Team sync with billing and security teams.

End of draft.
